title: Coffee, Not Coins
intro: Toddy matched with someone on the Spark dating app.
After Sophie, it's tempting to suspect everyone. But most people are just people.
Sniff carefully. Is this a con, or just a coffee?

msg.text: Hi! Loved your café photos ☕ Is that the place by the river?
Just so you know, I never talk money or crypto on here 😅
Want to meet for a coffee at a busy café on Saturday afternoon?
Bring a friend if you like!

verified.label: App-verified photo
verified.lens: Spark itself checked the photo matches the person.
verified.why: The app's own check is stronger evidence than any claim.

match.label: Mutual match
match.lens: You both liked each other in the app.
match.why: You chose to connect. He didn't come out of nowhere.

compliment.label: Compliment
compliment.lens: He noticed something real from your photos.
compliment.why: Friendly and specific. Normal on a dating app.

nomoney.label: No money talk
nomoney.lens: He says he never talks money on dating apps.
nomoney.why: The opposite of what a romance-investment scammer wants.

public.label: Meet in public
public.lens: A busy café, in the afternoon.
public.why: Meeting in a public place is what safety guides recommend.

friend.label: Bring a friend
friend.lens: He invites you to bring a friend.
friend.why: Scammers try to isolate you. This does the opposite.

avatar.label: Profile picture
avatar.why: Proves nothing alone, but the app verified it.

actions.label: Reply and meet at the busy café
Suggest a quick video call first

go_ahead.line: Saturday coffee was lovely. Marco never mentioned money once.

verify.line: A two-minute video call, then coffee. Careful and kind.

ignore.line: Nothing bad happened. It was just a real person saying hi.

block_report.line: Marco was real. When we treat everyone as a scammer, the real scams get lost in the noise.

what_if.block_report: Nothing here asked for money, secrecy or a move to another app. Those are the signs that matter.
what_if.ignore: Ignoring was safe. But nothing here was a warning sign: public meeting, no money talk, app-verified.

golden_rule: Watch what people ask for, not how friendly they are. No money, no secrecy, meet in public: that's what genuine looks like.

quick_check.q: Which of these is the strongest sign Marco is genuine?

options.text: He asked for nothing and suggested meeting in public
He has a nice profile picture

quick_check.explain: Compliments and photos can be faked. Asking for nothing and meeting in public is hard for a scammer to fake.

hints.nudge: What is Marco actually asking for?

rows.v: Spark matched the photo to the person
Liked each other in the app
A busy café, in the afternoon
He never does it on dating apps
